native.kind: new QNX guest execution observed during browser capture

environment.measurement: Guest monotonic clock under software emulation

captions.text: This is a new execution of the native C program in QNX 8 under QEMU. The browser observes the live guest serial stream.
QEMU boots QNX. The guest runs seven scenarios; the host then checks the raw console, event invariants and source digests.
All seven native scenarios passed, including zero-output containment after the restart budget was exhausted. Both guest and host exited successfully.
Recovery Lab replays native QNX 8 recordings. The worker proposes values; the supervisor owns the simulated output.
The first fresh proposal is accepted, but output remains zero.
The second proposal still keeps the output at zero.
The third fresh proposal completes validation and releases a valid output.
The worker now announces an injected out-of-range command.
Proposed output 999 is rejected. The supervisor holds the accepted output at zero.
The hold is a separate recorded decision, even when events share a timestamp.
A replacement worker starts as generation 2. Output remains zero.
The replacement must provide fresh proposal one.
Fresh proposal two still does not release the output.
Fresh proposal three restores the output. The guest timestamp records the observed recovery.
In this recording: 11 ms from fault notice to hold, then 280 ms to validated resume. No restarts means lockout.
Range checking alone is not enough. This injection repeats an old sequence number.
The duplicate sequence is rejected even though its numeric value is within range.
The replayed command never reaches the simulated output.
Next, the active worker deliberately sends generation zero.
Received generation zero does not match active generation one. The message is rejected and output is zero.
The validated replacement can resume output.
Repeated crashes exercise the restart budget.
The guest records the worker exit with code 42.
The supervisor holds zero before restarting.
A restart consumes one unit of the budget.
Fresh validation permits the replacement to run.
A second crash repeats the containment and recovery path.
The third crash arrives after both permitted restarts have been used.
The budget is exhausted. The supervisor stays locked out at zero.
The second recording keeps the same fault sequence and watchdog, with no restarts allowed.
Under that policy, the first rejected command holds zero without creating a replacement.
The first detected fault ends in containment: generation one, zero restarts, output zero.
Both recordings contain seven checked scenarios. Raw guest logs, source snapshots and digests are included. Output is simulated; QEMU timing is not a hardware guarantee.
